frameworks.name: Behavioral Definition Framework
frameworks.definition: A method for making abstract concepts operationally precise by translating emotional language into observable, measurable behaviors that any external observer could verify.

claims.text: The ability to predict what will happen next determines life outcomes; the better someone gets at prediction, the more they will achieve what they want. This requires an accurate framework of how reality works.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Accurate prediction requires an accurate mental model of reality; without it, people cannot rebuild from losses or repeat successes because they confuse luck with systematic understanding.

claims.text: Most people regurgitate and parrot information they have never thought deeply about, using words they do not understand. When asked to define their own statements or goals, they cannot provide coherent definitions.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: Removing sentiment, emotion, and psychology from analysis and using only a behaviorist frame (asking "what can I observe?") is the single greatest tool for defining reality accurately.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: Most people cannot communicate effectively because they use undefined terms. When two people exchange words neither has defined, they are relying on chance ("rolling the dice") to get what they want, which is why most people do not get what they want.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Undefined terms prevent shared understanding; lack of shared understanding makes goal achievement random rather than systematic.

claims.text: Defining terms at the beginning—as every legal document does with its recitation of definitions—is required to be precise about what you want and to enable effective communication.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: Abstract emotional language ("be more loving toward me") must be translated into observable behaviors ("give me a hug when I walk in the door") that can be verified by an external observer, such as a court witness.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: Bringing all communication down to observable reality and reaching agreement on what is observable is the foundation of distinguishing one's content and insights from other speakers' content, even when the underlying insights are the same.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: Selling is defined as increasing the likelihood that someone makes a purchasing decision. This is the sole job of a salesperson—to increase the probability of a purchasing decision by affecting observable variables that influence that percentage.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
bounded_by: Does not include non-observable factors like 'manifestation', 'synchronicity', or 'energy'—only variables that can be measured and influenced

claims.text: Using shorthand language (metaphorical or abstract phrasing) is faster for transferring ideas between people, but when neither party has defined the terms, it creates miscommunication and prevents effective execution.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Undefined shorthand creates shared illusion of understanding (both parties nod along) but masks actual lack of definition, leading to execution failure.

claims.text: To be an accurate communicator, terms must be defined before engagement in the conversation. This is annoying for some but is required for effective communication, especially in sales contexts.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: Focusing exclusively on the observable world and removing explanations based on non-observable phenomena significantly improves both predictive ability and life quality.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

examples.text: When a salesman is told 'sales is a transference of belief over a bridge of trust', it sounds compelling and visual. But when asked to execute—'How do I transfer belief over a bridge of trust? Who's got a bridge?'—the vague metaphor provides no actionable steps. The phrase sounds meaningful but is empty of observable definition.

A husband tells his wife 'I'd like you to be more loving toward me.' The wife cannot act on this because 'more loving' is undefined. Once translated to 'when I walk in the door, give me a hug', it becomes observable and actionable—a court witness could verify that the behavior occurred or did not occur.

An employee is given feedback 'do better work' but doesn't improve. Once the feedback is made observable—'follow this checklist, complete steps in this order, measure this metric'—behavior changes because the definition is clear.

practices.text: Begin every book, contract, and important communication with a recitation of defined terms. Make precision about what you want and what you mean non-negotiable.
When defining success, define what a win looks like, what success looks like, and what a fail looks like explicitly, down to granular observable behaviors.
In sales conversations, replace metaphors and abstract language with observable definitions of what you are asking the customer to do or decide.
When communicating a goal or expectation, ask the other person to translate it into observable behavior ('If I do X, can you observe that?') to ensure mutual understanding.
Focus on variables in the sales process that can be observed and measured; ignore factors that cannot be directly measured or influenced.
